title: I Want a Principle Within
description: I Want a Principle Within in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 224, “Watchfulness”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I want a prin-ci-ple with-in Of jeal-ous, god-ly fear; A sen-si-bil-i-ty to sin, A pain to find it near.

lines: A pain to find it near.
I want the first approach to feel
To catch the wandering of my will,
From Thee that I no more may part,
The filial awe, the fleshly heart,
Quick as the apple of an eye,
Awake my soul, when sin is nigh,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
